questions.qText: 1. Where are the protons and neutrons strictly located within an atom?
options: Embedded within the electron cloud to neutralize repulsive forces.
Orbiting the central core in fixed circular shells.
Nucleus
Randomly distributed throughout the empty space of the atom.

questions.qText: 2. What is the relative electrical charge of an electron?
options: +1, because it carries positive electrical current.
It varies depending on the isotope.
0, as its mass is too small to carry a measurable charge.

questions.qText: 3. What is the correct definition of the nucleon number (mass number)?
options: The number of valence electrons in the outermost shell.
The number of neutrons only.
The total sum of protons, neutrons, and electrons.
Protons plus neutrons.

questions.qText: 4. What strictly defines the proton number (atomic number) of an element?
options: The total number of nucleons present in the central nucleus.
The number of electron shells occupied by the atom.
The sum of the positively charged protons and negatively charged electrons.
Number of protons.

questions.qText: 5. In a neutral atom, which two subatomic particles must always be equal in number?
options: Protons and electrons.
Nucleon number and proton number.
Protons and neutrons.
Neutrons and electrons.

questions.qText: 6. Which subatomic particle has a relative mass of 1 and a relative charge of +1?
options: Neutron, because it balances electrostatic forces.
Nucleon, which occasionally escapes during bonding.
Proton
Electron, assuming it is composed of positron materials.

questions.qText: 7. What is the overall electrical charge of the nucleus?
options: Positive
Negative, because electrons overwhelm the protons.
Neutral, because protons are canceled by neutrons.
Zero, assuming it is devoid of charged particles.

questions.qText: 8. What is the electronic configuration of a neutral sodium atom (proton number 11)?
options: 2, 8, 2, because sodium is an alkaline earth metal.
2, 9, assuming the second shell expands.
2, 8, 8, allowing sodium to bypass the fourth shell.

questions.qText: 9. What is the maximum number of electrons that can fit into the first electron shell?
options: 18, assuming it contains s, p, and d sub-orbitals.
32, based on the formula 2n².
8, because all shells hold a full octet.

questions.qText: 10. What does the Period number of an element strictly indicate?
options: Number of electron shells.
The total number of protons and neutrons.
The total number of stable isotopes.
The number of valence electrons.

questions.qText: 11. What does the Group number (for main group elements) tell us about an atom?
options: Outer shell electrons.
The number of completely empty electron shells.
The exact number of neutrons in the most abundant isotope.
The total number of occupied electron shells.

questions.qText: 12. Which element is located in Period 3 and Group 2?
options: Calcium, assuming period is determined by atomic mass.
Magnesium
Beryllium, because it is the second element.
Sodium, because it is the first metal in the third period.

questions.qText: 13. Which noble gas has the exact electronic configuration of 2, 8?
options: Argon, assuming noble gases in Period 3 possess 10 electrons.
Neon
Krypton, forgetting to account for the valence electron.
Helium, possessing a full outer shell of 8 plus 2 inner.

questions.qText: 14. An atom has a nucleon number of 19 and a proton number of 9. How many neutrons does it have?
options: 19, representing the total count of neutrons.
9, assuming it must have equal neutrons and protons.
28, adding the atomic and mass numbers together.

questions.qText: 15. What strictly happens when a neutral sodium atom forms a sodium ion (Na⁺)?
options: Gains an electron shell to accommodate the positive charge.
Gains a proton to create a stable cation.
Loses one neutron, transforming into a different element.
Loses one electron.

questions.qText: 16. What is the electronic configuration of a chloride ion (Cl⁻)? (Note: Neutral Chlorine is 2,8,7)
options: 2, 8, 8, 1, placing the extra electron in a new fourth shell.
2, 8, 7, as the gain only affects inner core shells.
2, 8, 6, losing a proton to accommodate negative charge.

questions.qText: 17. Which statement correctly defines isotopes?
options: Atoms with the same mass number but different electronic configurations.
Molecules with the same number of atoms but different geometries.
Same protons, different neutrons.
Atoms with the same number of neutrons but different protons.

questions.qText: 18. Why do two different isotopes of the same element undergo the exact same chemical reactions?
options: Same valence electrons.
The strong nuclear force is identical, preventing external reactions.
They have identical nucleon numbers, exerting the same gravitational pull.
Their nuclei possess the exact same number of neutrons.

options: 6 protons, 8 neutrons, 6 electrons
6 protons, 6 neutrons, 6 electrons
8 protons, 6 neutrons, 8 electrons
14 protons, 14 neutrons, 14 electrons

questions.qText: 21. What is the charge of an ion that has 11 protons and 10 electrons?
22. Which of the following pairs represents isotopes of the same element?
options: ¹²C and ¹⁴C
¹⁴C and ¹⁴N
H₂O and D₂O
O₂ and O₃

questions.qText: 23. The relative atomic mass of Chlorine is 35.5. What does this indicate about its isotopes?
options: Chlorine atoms have exactly 35.5 neutrons.
It is a weighted average of Cl-35 and Cl-37 isotopes.
Chlorine only exists as a single isotope with a mass of 35.5.
The proton number of chlorine is 35.5.

questions.qText: 24. An element X has the electronic configuration 2, 8, 3. Which of the following is true about element X?
options: It is a non-metal in Group 3.
It is a metal in Period 3, Group 13 (or III).
It is a noble gas.
It forms an ion with a -3 charge.
